newsitem.title: CHINA: China cracks down on accounting fraud.
newsitem.headline: China cracks down on accounting fraud.

text.p: China's Ministry of Finance reported initial success in its three-month-old campaign to clean up the fraud-ridden accounting industry, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
Spot-checks of nearly 840,000 accounting offices revealed that 16 percent of the examined offices held false accounts containing more than 14 billion yuan, it said.
The ministry fined 70,000 offices, disqualified more than 200 accountants, and filed charges against 46, it said.
Major offences included false accounts, fabricating information and keeping disorderly accounts, Xinhua quoted a ministry official as saying.
China's accounting practices lag behind international standards, but new regulations were expected later this year from the ministry and the China Securities Regulatory Commission.
An audit of 178,000 government units last year turned up 203.8 billion yuan in illegal funds, up 100 percent from 1995.
